body.goal: Replace src/taskops/ui/index.html (357-line vanilla prototype) with a React+TypeScript dashboard styled after the Nova design concept (~/Desktop/Agent collaboration dashboard/Taskops Nova.dc.html): dark/light token system, chrome with tabs + KPI rail, attention groups as the landing, a kanban board, a card dossier drawer, and an hours view. Served exactly as today: `taskops ui` → http/server → GET /<board>/ui/* from src/taskops/ui/ (committed bundle, no node at install time). Data: POST /<board>/rpc {verb,args} with envelope {ok,seq,data}, verbs `board`/`card`/`report`/`mentions` for reads, `update` (comment only) as the ONE write; GET /<board>/feed WebSocket (SSE fallback) as a SIGNAL that triggers debounced refetch, never a payload.
rules: The UI is read-only about everything it SHOWS except ONE write: the comment box (update with comment=, mentions=). No status buttons, no take, no merge from the browser — a second way to move a card is a second way for the two to disagree (see the header comment of the current src/taskops/ui/index.html — that contract survives the rewrite).

Dev source lives in ui/ at the repo root; the build output (index.html, app.js, style.css) is COMMITTED into src/taskops/ui/ so `pip install taskops` serves a dashboard with no node toolchain. React is bundled, never a CDN. Copy v1's closure: `npm run check` = typecheck + build + smoke + `git diff --exit-code src/taskops/ui`.
The feed socket is a signal, not data: every frame triggers a debounced (~150ms) refetch of `board` (+ the open card). Never render from a frame.

The wire is only POST <base>/rpc with {verb, args} and Authorization: Bearer <token> (?token= bootstrap into localStorage like today), answers are {ok,seq,data}|{ok:false,error:{code,message}}. Only verbs board/card/report/mentions/update exist for this client — do not invent routes or verbs.

Nova's token system is the palette: copy the [data-tk=dark]/[data-tk=light] custom-property blocks from Taskops Nova.dc.html into ui/src/theme/tokens.css verbatim (Inter + JetBrains Mono, --canvas/--pane/--accent/--ok/--warn/--danger...). All component styling through those vars.

esbuild, not Vite: ui/build.mjs mirrors v1's (~/taskops/ui/build.mjs) — esm, es2022, minified, no sourcemap, entry ui/src/main.tsx, css bundle, index.html copied. No router library and no state library: views are state in main.tsx, one custom hook owns fetching (v1's useStudio shape).

python ./scripts/lint and ./scripts/test must stay green; tests/test_architecture.py rules (imports down, ≤200 lines) apply to src/taskops python — the ui/ TS source is outside its scope but keep files small and cohesive anyway.
Docs are part of the diff: README serving section, CLAUDE.md 'What is left', ARCHITECTURE.md if the ui layer description changes.

card.spec:
Write `docs/fan-out.md`: the post-mortem of THIS milestone and what taskops should do about it. Same register as `docs/design.md` and `docs/implement-reviewer.md` — a forensic account with file:line evidence, not advice. It is the paper trail for a decision not yet taken; it must be arguable, and it must be honest about what each proposal costs.

## The facts (verify every one; do not take this spec's word)

Eight cards, eight workers, eight worktrees. Zero merge conflicts, zero stale leases, no `recover` needed — the coordination mechanism did its whole job. And yet the merged tree had:

1. **Two `ago()`** with different output (`just now`/`5m ago` vs `45s`/`5m`), fixed by tk-ab86b6 into `ui/src/format.ts`.
2. **Three `initials()`** — STILL PRESENT at the time of writing: `ui/src/format.ts:45` (2 chars upper), `ui/src/pages/Hours.tsx:256` (2 chars lower), `ui/src/components/chrome/AvatarStack.tsx:11` as `initial` (1 char upper). The header therefore renders eight identical "W" avatars for w1..w8. Read AvatarStack's own docstring above the function: it reasons about exactly this failure ("a stack of five 'A's would say nothing") and then walks into its own version of it.
3. **Six green cards and a placeholder page.** App.tsx (tk-4e0fdb) documented a slot contract in a COMMENT; the three pages were built in parallel against that prose. `<HoursPage report=… />` in the comment vs `Hours({client})` in the code. Nobody could compare them: a comment is not typechecked. Fixed by tk-aa77c1, a card that did not exist when the milestone was planned.

**The control that proves the cause**: `ui/src/types.ts` has ONE definition of each type, imported by 9 files, zero duplication. Same eight agents, same session, same instructions. The difference is that `types.ts` was landed by a SERIALIZED card (tk-5341aa) before the fan-out, and `format.ts` did not exist when the four parallel workers branched. Search cannot find what is being written concurrently in another branch.

## Why the board's existing warning could not see it

Read `src/taskops/verbs/_context.py:64` — `collisions()` intersects the DECLARED `files` of open cards with a holder. The four fan-out cards declared disjoint paths, so the intersection was empty and the warning was correctly silent. The failure was never same-file: it was four different files carrying the same concept. Collision detection lives in path space; this class of failure lives in symbol space. State that plainly — it is the sharpest sentence in the document.

## The four causes, argued

1. Parallel agents search correctly and correctly find nothing (structural, not negligence — CLAUDE.md's "search first" was obeyed).
2. A seam expressed as prose cannot be checked; expressed as a type it is a compile error in every worktree at once.
3. Every card's acceptance criteria measured its own part. Not one measured the whole, so green summed to a placeholder.
4. The merged tree has no reader until the orchestrator looks. Each worker verified in a worktree where its file was the only new one; the duplication exists ONLY in the integration branch, a place no worker ever sees.

## The proposals — rank them, and argue the cost of each

Evaluate against this repo's stated allergies (ARCHITECTURE.md §11, CLAUDE.md "never re-introduce"): no stored derived state, no repair verbs, no roles, no hook that decides.

- **A. A merge-time symbol report.** `taskops_merge task=` already runs in the integration worktree with the whole merged tree present. After a clean merge it could name exported symbols that now have more than one definition among the milestone's touched files — derived, read-only, nothing stored, and it is precisely the "second reader" the merged tree never had. **Argue the real objection honestly**: taskops is language-agnostic today, and a symbol scanner is not. Does this belong in the tool, in an optional per-project hook, or in `taskops tidy`? Do not pretend the objection is small; it may sink the proposal, and the document should say so if it does.
- **B. Milestone acceptance criteria.** Cards have `criteria`; a Milestone (`core/types.py:94`) has `goal` and `rules` and nothing that says what the CHAPTER is accepted against. "The served page renders all three tabs against a real board" is a milestone criterion, and it is what makes six-green-cards-and-a-placeholder impossible to ignore. `merge milestone=` already refuses while a card is open; it could show these and require the human to answer them. Same shape as `rules` — spec, not status.
- **C. A plan-time shape warning.** `plan` sees the whole tree in one call. N cards with no `after` between them whose `files` share a directory prefix IS a fan-out onto a shared surface with no foundation card. Warn in the answer; never refuse. Assess the false-positive risk — a warning nobody believes is worse than none.
- **D. Walking-skeleton ordering.** Free, and no code: land scaffold + shell + ONE page wired end to end BEFORE fanning out. Every later seam then exists as a type, and every later card plugs into something that runs. Note that this milestone did exactly this for types and got zero duplication there — D is the generalisation of the one thing that worked.

End with a recommendation, not a menu. If the honest answer is "D is free and A/B/C are not worth their cost", say that.

This card is `no_code` if you only write the document — but you must still verify every file:line claim above against the tree, and correct any that has drifted. A post-mortem that misquotes its own evidence is worse than none.

card.spec:
`docs/fan-out.md` is the post-mortem of this milestone: eight parallel cards, zero merge conflicts, and a merged tree that still came back with two `ago()`, three `initials()` and three pages built against a prose contract that had not been merged yet. Its conclusion was **D** (land the shared seams SERIALIZED before any fan-out) and **B** (milestones need acceptance criteria), rejecting a symbol scanner and a plan-time path heuristic.

The problem now is that the document is FILED, not OPERATIVE. A lesson in `docs/` is read by whoever already went looking. The whole architecture of this project says context must travel in the ANSWER, not wait in a file (`CLAUDE.md` "idea 4": the MCP `instructions`, `taskops_board`, and the pulse line). This card puts the lesson on that path.

Read first, and treat them as the constraints: `docs/fan-out.md` (the argument), `ARCHITECTURE.md` §11/§14 (the allergies), `CLAUDE.md` "never re-introduce", `src/taskops/mcp/server.py::INSTRUCTIONS`, `src/taskops/verbs/plan.py`, `src/taskops/verbs/assign.py`, `src/taskops/core/types.py::Milestone`, `src/taskops/verbs/_context.py::collisions`.

**Two pieces of work:**

1. **B — milestone acceptance criteria.** `Milestone` (core/types.py:94) stores `goal`, `rules`, `reviews`, `branch`, and nothing that says what the CHAPTER is accepted against. Cards have `criteria`; a chapter does not, which is why six green cards summed to a placeholder page and nobody was refused anything. Add `criteria: list[str]` beside `rules` — same shape, same lifetime, spec not status. Accept it in `plan` (and in `update milestone=`, the way `rules` is replaced whole), carry it into what a worker sees the way `rules` travels, and render it where the chapter is judged: `merge milestone=` already refuses while a card is open or unintegrated, so it must SHOW these and make the human answer them. It must not become a stored status or a gate the machine decides — the human decides; the board records.

2. **D — the ordering rule, delivered.** Put it where a planner reads it at the moment of planning, not in a file they might open: the MCP instructions and/or what `plan` answers. The rule in one sentence: *the shared vocabulary — types, formatting helpers, prop interfaces — lands in ONE serialized card before any fan-out, because parallel workers branch from a common ancestor and cannot search for what does not exist yet.* Keep it SHORT: `mcp/hello.py` exists because the handshake payload has a hard budget, and a paragraph that pushes the board out of the greeting costs more than it teaches.

**Do not** widen `collisions()`, add a language parser, add a repair verb, or add a hook that decides — `docs/fan-out.md` argues each of those down and `ARCHITECTURE.md` §11 bans the shapes. If while implementing you conclude the document was WRONG about one of them, do not quietly do it anyway: say so in your close note with the argument, and leave it undone.

Every new rule needs a test — `tests/test_architecture.py`'s own principle is that a rule with no test is a suggestion. Update `docs/fan-out.md` itself to record what was adopted and where it is enforced, so the paper trail does not end at the recommendation.

BLOCKED ON THE BASE BRANCH — not on the design. My worktree has no `ui/` at all.

Evidence (run in /Users/berna/taskops-v2):

    $ git rev-parse --short master ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova
    9260df4   master
    9260df4   ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel
    afd6e95   ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova

    $ git ls-tree master --name-only
    .gitignore ARCHITECTURE.md CLAUDE.md MENTIONS.md README.md docs pyproject.toml scripts src tests uv.lock
    # no ui/

    $ git merge-base --is-ancestor ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel
    NOT an ancestor
    $ git rev-list --count ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel..ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova
    27

`ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel` was branched from `master`, and `ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova` (27 commits: `ui/src/types.ts`, `ui/src/format.ts`, `ui/src/theme/tokens.css`, `components/chrome|board|card`, `pages/Board.tsx`, `docs/fan-out.md`) has never landed on `master`. So `.taskops/trees/tk-07ff97/` contains: ARCHITECTURE.md CLAUDE.md MENTIONS.md README.md docs pyproject.toml scripts src tests uv.lock — and nothing else. `ui/` does not exist, `docs/fan-out.md` does not exist there either (it is on the ui branch), and `npm ci` has nothing to run in.

Every one of my four deliverables sits inside `ui/src/`: Pane.tsx, pages/Monitor.tsx, components/monitor/panels.ts (which must import `BoardPayload`/`ReportPayload` from `ui/src/types.ts`), and the TabNav mount (`ui/src/components/chrome/TabNav.tsx`). I cannot write any of them here without either (a) re-creating types.ts / tokens.css / format.ts / TabNav from scratch — which is precisely the duplication this SEAM card exists to prevent, and which would collide head-on when the ui milestone lands — or (b) running `git merge ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova` myself, which a worker may never do.

I did NOT touch the tree. Nothing was written, nothing was merged.

The fix is yours, one of two moves:
1. Land the ui milestone first — `taskops_merge milestone=ui-react-dashboard-nova` — then re-cut `ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel` (and `tk-07ff97`) from the new `master`; or
2. Re-base the monitor milestone branch onto `ms/ui-react-dashboard-nova` if the ui chapter is not ready for `main` yet.

Either way the five blocked panel cards (tk-db88c4, tk-c22565, tk-f38042, tk-60334f, tk-4b37dd) inherit the same wrong base and would each hit this — better it is fixed once, here, before dispatch.

Design read confirms the card is otherwise buildable: `~/Desktop/Agent collaboration dashboard/Taskops Nova.dc.html` lines 168-417 are intact and I have transcribed the grid ratios, paddings, radii and the five subtitle strings. Hand the card back with a correct base and I land it without further questions.

body.text:
Confirmed, and you were right to write nothing. The diagnosis is exact and the fault is mine: I planned this milestone while the entire UI chapter sat unmerged, so `base_ref` cut the branch from `master` (9260df4) — which has no `ui/` — instead of from the tree the panels build on. The two paths you offered are the only two, and I am taking the decision to Berna because landing a milestone into the trunk is the human's explicit call, never the orchestrator's.

Two facts that make the repair cheap, both verified:
  git rev-list --count master..ms/monitor-nova-panel-by-panel  →  0
  git rev-list --count master..tk-07ff97                       →  0
Neither branch carries a commit, so once the UI chapter lands, both fast-forward onto the new trunk with nothing to merge and nothing to lose. Your worktree stays where it is; it simply gains `ui/`.

Refusing to re-create types.ts, tokens.css and format.ts was the whole job here. This card exists to stop parallel workers inventing the same thing twice, and a SEAM card that started by duplicating the vocabulary it was meant to publish would have been the purest possible version of the failure `docs/fan-out.md` describes — and it would have collided head-on with 27 commits the moment the UI chapter landed. Reporting beat delivering.

Stay put. When the base is fixed I hand this card straight back with the same spec, and your transcription of Nova 168-417 — the grid ratios, paddings, radii and the five verbatim subtitles — is exactly what it needs, so none of that reading is wasted.

card.spec:
**Note: this card is a repo-wide documentation sweep. The milestone's Nova-transcription rules do not apply to it** — it is filed here only because this is the open chapter.

"Docs must not lie" is a stated rule of this project and several statements have expired. Fix every one, and verify each claim against the code rather than against this list — this spec was written from a quick audit and may itself be incomplete or already wrong.

**Known stale, all confirmed by running the counts:**
- `README.md:11` says the management interface is "**eight** tools" while `README.md:172` heads a section "The **nine** tools". One file, two answers. The truth is nine: assign, board, card, comment, merge, plan, review, take, update (`grep -oE '"taskops_[a-z]+"' src/taskops/mcp/tools.py | sort -u`).
- `CLAUDE.md:5` and `ARCHITECTURE.md:5` both say "67 files / ~6,500 lines". Actual: 68 Python files, 6,726 lines under `src/taskops`. More importantly BOTH counts silently exclude the dashboard, which is now 23 TypeScript files under `ui/src` plus the committed bundle — a real part of this repo that the headline description of the repo does not mention. Decide whether the count means Python-only (then say so explicitly) or the whole source (then include the UI), and make both files agree.

**Then sweep for the rest.** The repo has changed a great deal in one session: the vanilla single-file page became a built React app; `Milestone.criteria` and the serialize-the-seams rule were added; `docs/fan-out.md` was written; an Attention screen and an Hours tab were built and then removed; the UI chapter landed into master. Anything describing any of that in the wrong tense, or describing a screen that no longer exists, or a count, or a "not yet"/"pending"/status table, is in scope. `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `MENTIONS.md` and the files in `docs/` are all in scope.

**Two traps:**
1. **Monitor is being built RIGHT NOW** by a sibling worker (card tk-07ff97, then five panel cards). It does NOT exist yet. Describe the dashboard as it is at the moment you write — Board plus the card dossier drawer — and do not write it up as though Monitor had landed. Writing tomorrow's truth is the same defect as leaving yesterday's.
2. Do not touch `ui/`, `src/taskops/*.py` or `tests/` except to READ them. Your surface is documentation. A sibling is in `ui/` and `App.tsx` right now.

Where a doc states a rule that a test enforces, check the test still exists and still enforces it — `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s table of rules names its test in the right-hand column, and a row naming a test that no longer exists is the worst kind of stale because it reads as a guarantee.

- Shape: `Event[]` verbatim from core/types.py — id, task, actor, kind, body (open dict, unknown kinds intact), ts. `task` included and NOT filtered: "project" carries the board-level facts and this pane is board-wide. ui/src/types.ts::Event already matches; nothing new to type.

- Counter: the verb also returns the log's TOTAL length, an int, for the header's mono counter. `total` is separate from the page because the counter means "how many events exist", not "how many were sent".
- Paging: keyset, never offset. `before=<ts>` returns the `limit` events strictly older than that instant; the caller passes back the `ts` of the last row it received. Offset paging skips or repeats rows as the log grows under a reader, and this log only ever grows at the head.
- Optional narrowing, if wanted: `task=` for one card (that is the dossier's history and already exists), `kinds=[...]`. Neither is needed for this pane.

## 2. The `review` row Nova draws and this pane cannot — the spec, so nobody rediscovers it

Nova's `procs` has FIVE rows and three states, not two: `doing` (OK), **`review` (WARN)** and `stalled` (DANGER). Design line 1168:

```
mk('tk-771088', 'VAT calculator', 'agent:berna/rv1', '4m 30s', 'review', 'review', WARN, 'var(--warn-soft)', 'var(--warn-soft)', 5.8, 19, false, 3)
```

Note what that row is: `remainLabel: 'review'`, actor `rv1`, and a lease with **4m 30s left**. That is not a card sitting in the `review` group waiting for somebody — it is a card a VERIFIER is actively holding. The board's own word for it is `reviewing`: "a verifier holds a live REVIEW lease" (CLAUDE.md), a second mutex in `live.sqlite` (`store/reviews.py`). It is a LIVE LEASE, which is precisely what this pane is about, and it is the only one of the three states currently invisible here.

What widening the seam takes, exactly:

**`panels.ts`** — one field on `LiveLeasesProps`, between `doing` and `stalled` (that is also its render order in the design):

```ts

   *  second mutex, not the `review` group: `review` is handed-in-and-waiting
   *  (no lease, nothing to count down), `reviewing` is somebody running. */
  reviewing: readonly BoardRow[];
```

**`Monitor.tsx`** — one prop at line 93:

```tsx
<LiveLeases doing={g.doing} reviewing={g.reviewing} stalled={g.stalled} now={now} onOpen={openCard} />
```

**The data is already on the wire.** `BoardPayload.groups` carries `reviewing` today — I confirmed it against the live board at `http://127.0.0.1:54546`; the `board` verb returned `{'merge': 0, 'mentions': 0, 'review': 0, 'changes': 0, 'stalled': 0, 'take': 0, 'doing': 6, 'reviewing': 0, 'blocked': 0}`. It is `readonly BoardRow[]`, the same shape as `doing` (`holder`, `since`, `quiet_for`), so no new row type is needed — the reviewing rows carry the reviewer as `holder`, which is the actor Nova prints (`rv1`).

**Inside LiveLeases** it is then ~4 lines and NO new machinery, because `held()` already computes everything a live lease needs:

```ts
function reviewing_(row: BoardRow, now: number): LeaseProc {
  return { ...held(row, now), remainLabel: "review", state: "review", tone: "warn" };
}
```

and one more spread in the `rows` array, between doing and stalled. `level()` already branches on `p.state === "doing"`, so a `review` row would currently fall into the silence branch — that condition must become "has a live lease" (`doing` or `review`) when the prop lands. That is the one line in my file a widener has to touch, and I am flagging it rather than pre-writing dead code for a prop that does not exist.

Whoever picks it up owns `panels.ts` + `Monitor.tsx`; I did not touch either.

card.spec:
The Throughput pane is correctly built and can never show data as wired. Verified end to end against the live board:

- `src/taskops/verbs/pulse.py:87` — `"hours": _hours(stores, args, now, window) if window else None`. The board payload carries `hours` ONLY when the call passes `window=`.
- `ui/src/pages/Monitor.tsx:96` — `<Throughput report={board.hours} />`.
- `ui/src/useBoard.ts` calls `rpc('board', {})` with no arguments.

So `board.hours` is always `null`, and Throughput always renders its empty state. Proof, same board, one call apart: `board {}` → `hours: None`; `board {window:'14d', tz:'Europe/Madrid'}` → 14 days, `total {seconds: 10388, closed: 20}`.

Nobody did anything wrong on the way here — the pane was built and tested against report data its own probe fetched, and the seam wired it to a real field. What nobody checked is that the field is conditional. That is the seam defect this chapter is supposed to be immune to, one level below where we were looking.

**The fix is the argument, and the judgement is where the window comes from.** Two candidates, and pick deliberately rather than by convenience:

1. `useBoard` always sends `window` + `tz` on its `board` call. Cheapest, but it makes every board fetch do the hours arithmetic — including on the Board tab, which does not use it, and on every socket-triggered refetch. Read `verbs/report.py::summary` and `core/hours.py` to judge what that costs per call before choosing it.
2. Throughput owns its own `report` fetch, the way the deleted Hours page did — Monitor already receives the client. Keeps the board call cheap and gives the pane a window switcher later, at the cost of a second round trip and a second loading state.

Whichever you choose, say why on the card, and make `ThroughputProps` honest about it — if the pane fetches for itself, `report` should not be a prop that lies about where the data comes from. Changing `panels.ts` or `Monitor.tsx` IS allowed here: the five panel workers are done and this card owns the seam.

The browser must send a real IANA timezone (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`), never a hardcoded UTC — the hours are bucketed by calendar day and the wrong zone silently shifts every bar.

While you are in there, check the same class of bug on the other panes: any prop wired to a payload field that is conditional, optional or only populated under an argument. `board.hours` was one; say whether there are others.

body.subject: the one fetcher asks for the window, so Throughput has days to draw

body.reason:
Verified the spec's chain myself before touching anything, and it holds exactly as written: pulse.py:87 `"hours": _hours(...) if window else None`, Monitor.tsx:96 `<Throughput report={board.hours} />`, useBoard.ts `rpc("board", {})`. Re-proved against the live board on 54546 (board slug is `board`, not `api`):

    board {}                          -> hours = None
    board {window:14d,tz:Europe/Madrid} -> days 14, total {'seconds': 10528.4, 'closed': 20}

CHOICE (criterion 2): option 1 — the ONE fetcher asks for the window, always. Not for cheapness of edit, but because useBoard.ts's own docstring is the rule: "There is exactly one owner of what the board says right now... a second component with its own effect would fetch on its own clock and paint a board half a second older than the one next to it." Option 2 puts Throughput's chart on a different snapshot than the rows beside it and makes every socket frame fan out to two fetchers instead of one coalesced refetch. The Hours page could own its fetch because it WAS the page; a pane inside Monitor is not.

Cost of option 1, measured not guessed. report.py::summary runs one cache.window over the whole span plus one per day (15 SQLite reads at 14d) and folds them through core/hours.py. Five curls each, same live board:

    board {}                     0.0046 0.0035 0.0032 0.0028 0.0027 s   8766 bytes
    board {window:14d,tz:...}    0.0040 0.0041 0.0044 0.0043 0.0041 s  14455 bytes

+~1.3ms and +5.7KB per refetch, on a call already coalesced to one per 150ms burst. Paid on the Board tab too — deliberately: making the args depend on the active tab would turn switching tabs into a refetch, which is worse than 1.3ms.

`ThroughputProps.report` stays a prop and its doc no longer lies — it now says the data DOES arrive as a prop because useBoard asks for it on the same snapshot, and that `null` is the fallback for a caller that forgot the argument, which is why the empty state still names it. Added THROUGHPUT_DAYS/THROUGHPUT_WINDOW to panels.ts: Throughput's `SLOT = VIEW_W / THROUGHPUT_DAYS` and useBoard's `window` now read the same 14, so the slot width and the requested window cannot drift.

CRITERION 3: `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, try/catch + `|| "UTC"` for a runtime with no zone data. The served bundle carries it — `curl .../board/ui/app.js | grep -o "resolvedOptions().timeZone"` hits, and `window:Lp,tz:ev()` is the minified call site.

CRITERION 4 — the audit, and the answer is: no others. I read pulse.py::run and _context.py against ui/src/types.ts and grepped every `board.`/`card.` consumer in ui/src.
- board payload: milestone, milestones, groups, team, hours, seq, pulse. `hours` was the ONLY argument-conditional one. `_which(stores, args)` takes an optional `milestone=` arg but falls back to `_facts.open_milestone`, so `board.milestone` is null from board STATE (no single open milestone), never from a missing argument — Chapter.tsx handles null and says so. Everything else is built unconditionally on every call.
- card payload consumers (Drawer/Sections): `standing`, `epic`, `lease`, `merged_into` are null from state (never submitted / no parent / nobody holds it), not from an argument. Honest nullability, handled.
- EventStream `events={[]}` and LeaseProc.load are the already-documented no-source gaps (panels.ts notes 1 and 3), not this class of defect.
- One nuance worth writing down rather than a bug: `groups.mentions` is per-READER (`_mentions(stores, actor)`), so the "Addressed to you" pane shows whatever actor the browser's token resolves to. Populated on every call, but its content depends on identity, not on an argument.

CRITERION 1 — proved by rendering the REAL Monitor with the REAL live payload. A throwaway harness (deleted, not committed) bundled `pages/Monitor.tsx` for node, fetched the board with exactly the args useBoard now sends, and rendered it with react-dom/server:

    board args -> {"window":"14d","tz":"Europe/Madrid"}
    hours is null? false
    days: 14 total: {"seconds":10528.42069530487,"closed":20}
    throughput <rect> count: 28 · day groups: 14
    footer totals: ["20","31","—"]
    empty state present? false
    OK: Throughput renders day bars against the live board

28 rects = two bars (commits + closes) on each of 14 days; footer is 20 cards closed, 31 commits, and `—` for reviews (the honest no-source cell the pane already had).

SERVING: started a second server from this worktree — `serve --root /Users/berna/taskops-v2/.taskops --port 54611`, never touching 54546 — so it serves MY bundle over the SAME live board. `GET /board/ui/ -> 200`, app.js 201622 bytes, contains the tz call and the window arg, and `POST /board/rpc` on that same process answers `days 14 {'seconds': 10528.4, 'closed': 20}`. Killed after. What I could NOT do is drive a real browser: there is no puppeteer/playwright/jsdom in ui/node_modules (react, react-dom, esbuild, typescript, @types only) and ui/smoke/ does not exist yet — that harness is still a card on the board. So the render proof is server-side React against live data, not a headless click-through; saying so plainly rather than implying more.

CRITERION 5: `npm run typecheck` clean; `node build.mjs` from ui/ (app.js 196.9kb, style.css 2.7kb) with src/taskops/ui/app.js committed; `./scripts/lint` -> "All checks passed! / 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations"; `./scripts/test` -> "202 passed, 1 skipped in 12.64s" — the baseline, unchanged.

`taskops_merge task=` attempts the merge and reports whatever git says. When the card's branch does not contain the milestone head, that is a CONFLICT message about a file — and the real cause (the branch is behind) is never named.       cd .taskops/trees/tk-xxxx && git merge ms/<slug>
    then taskops_merge task=tk-xxxx again

Include the commit count (`git rev-list --count`) — "behind" without a number reads as a bigger problem than it is.

card.spec:
`src/taskops/ui/app.js` is committed on purpose — that is what makes `pip install taskops` serve a dashboard with no node toolchain. But it is minified output, byte-different in every branch, so N parallel cards produce N-1 guaranteed conflicts, and every landing invalidates the remaining resolutions. This chapter paid roughly six round trips to it; three workers independently reached the same diagnosis on their cards.

Two fixes, and they are not exclusive:

1. **A merge driver.** The repo has no `.gitattributes`. A generated artifact should never be text-merged: mark `src/taskops/ui/*` so a conflict resolves by regeneration rather than by hunk. Investigate `merge=ours` plus a rebuild step versus a custom driver, and note that a driver needs `git config` per clone — which is a real cost for a tool other people install. Say which you chose and what it costs a fresh clone.
2. **A planning convention.** Panel cards should not each rebuild and commit the bundle; one card rebuilds at the end. Write it where a planner reads it — the same reasoning that put the serialize-the-seams rule in `mcp/server.py::INSTRUCTIONS`, and the same budget discipline: `mcp/hello.py` has a hard cap, so one sentence, not a paragraph.

Record the outcome in `docs/fan-out.md` — it is the paper trail for exactly this class of failure and this is a new instance with a different cause: not two workers writing the same concept, but N workers regenerating the same artifact.

body.subject: A generated artifact is rebuilt, never text-merged

body.reason:
Commit 66d9e88 (`Task: tk-cb8a8a`), 6 files: `.gitattributes` (new), `README.md`, `docs/fan-out.md`, `src/taskops/mcp/server.py`, `tests/test_architecture.py`, `tests/test_mcp.py`. Disjoint from b1 and b2 — I touched no gitwork/, no gitmoves, no verbs/plan.py, and no `ui/`.

## Both fixes, and the honest cost of each

**1. `.gitattributes` — `-diff -merge linguist-generated=true` on the three build outputs. I rejected the custom merge driver, and the reason is the one the spec anticipated.** A `[merge "ours"] driver = true` (or one shelling out to `node build.mjs`) is *local, per-clone config*: it cannot be committed, it silently does nothing in a clone that skipped `git config`, and for a tool people `pip install` that is a footgun bought for no gain. **`-merge` is built into git** — a fresh clone needs nothing, which is criterion 2 met by "nothing extra required" rather than by documentation (README says so anyway).

Measured in a scratch repo, 2026-08-08, both directions:
- *Same region touched by both branches.* Without the attribute git writes `<<<<<<<` markers **inside minified JavaScript**. With it: `warning: Cannot merge binary files` / `CONFLICT` / `UU`, our copy left **whole**, zero markers to accidentally commit.
- *Different regions* — the case nobody was watching, and the real reason the line exists. Two branches editing separated lines of the same generated file: **without the attribute git auto-merged SILENTLY** (`Merge made by the 'ort' strategy`, exit 0) into a file no build ever emitted. With the attribute: `CONFLICT`, every time. The six round trips this chapter paid were visible; a silently spliced bundle would not have been.

It does **not** auto-resolve, and cannot: a generated file has exactly one correct resolution and git cannot perform it. What it does is guarantee the merge stops and the only sane resolution is the rebuild.

Live in this repo — `git check-attr merge diff` on all three: `merge: unset`, `diff: unset` (i.e. both disabled) for `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`.

**2. The convention, one sentence, in `mcp/server.py::INSTRUCTIONS`** beside §10's ordering rule: "· and if that surface has a GENERATED artifact committed (a built bundle), ONE card rebuilds it at the end — N cards rebuilding it is N-1 conflicts by construction ·". INSTRUCTIONS is now **1876 chars against `hello.CAP = 2900`, leaving 1022 for the panorama** (the test's own floor is 300).

They are not alternatives: the convention removes the conflict from a *planned* fan-out; the attribute protects the unplanned one — a repair card, a rebase, a human rebuilding to check something — where no convention was written down.

## Criteria

1. **MET** — the conflict is never a hand-merge of minified JS: `-merge` leaves the file whole and the documented resolution is `cd ui && node build.mjs && git add ../src/taskops/ui && git commit --no-edit`. And the convention that prevents the situation is in INSTRUCTIONS, which every host loads at the handshake — exactly where §10 put the ordering rule.
2. **MET** — a fresh clone needs nothing: `-merge` is built-in, no driver, no `git config`. Documented in README anyway (`### Working on the dashboard itself`), including the resolution command.
3. **MET** — `docs/fan-out.md` **§11**, with the cause stated as distinct from §7's: there, two workers wrote the same *concept* in two files; here every worker wrote a different concept in a different file and then all five regenerated the same *artifact*. §10's ordering rule HELD — not one `.tsx` conflicted across five branches — and the chapter still paid ~6 round trips to one path. It records the three workers' converged recipe and the "bundle only grows" check verbatim, both measurements above, why the driver was rejected, and what neither fix covers (a branch that edits `ui/src` and forgets to rebuild still ships a stale dashboard — that is `npm run check`'s `git diff --exit-code`, unrelated). The doc header now points at §11.
4. **MET** — `./scripts/lint` → `All checks passed!` / `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`. `./scripts/test` → **207 passed, 1 skipped in 11.89s** (206 baseline + my one new test). Working tree clean after the mutation checks.

## Mutation-checked, both new pins

- `tests/test_architecture.py::test_the_committed_bundle_is_never_text_merged` — dropped `-merge` from the app.js line → `AssertionError: app.js may still be text-merged into a bundle no build produced / assert '-merge' in ['-diff', 'linguist-generated=true']`. Restored, green.
- `tests/test_mcp.py::test_the_instructions_carry_the_whole_protocol` (extended, not rewritten — I added two needles and touched none of the existing ones) — deleted the sentence from INSTRUCTIONS → `assert 'GENERATED artifact' in "…"` failed. Restored, green.

## FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR — what to do differently with the five queued UI cards

**Do not change how you dispatch them in parallel. Change who commits the bundle.**

- Dispatch the five panel cards as before — the seam is landed, their `.tsx` files are disjoint, and §10's rule is already proving itself: zero source conflicts across five branches this chapter.
- **Tell each panel card NOT to run `node build.mjs` and NOT to commit `src/taskops/ui/`.** Their criteria should keep `npm run typecheck` (that is what proves the panel compiles) and drop the build step. Their diff is then `.tsx` only, and every merge into `ms/…` is clean by construction — no round trip, no resolution to invalidate.
- **Add one last card, after all five, that only rebuilds**: `cd ui && node build.mjs`, commit `src/taskops/ui/`, and grep the bundle for a marker string from each of the five panels (`pane-*`) to prove all five are in it. That card is the *only* one whose surface includes the bundle. It is small, serialized, and it is where the "bundle only grows" check belongs.
- **If you keep the bundle in every card anyway** (e.g. a worker needs to eyeball the rendered page), the attribute now makes that survivable rather than dangerous: the merge stops loudly instead of splicing, and the recipe is one command. But it is still N-1 conflicts you no longer have to pay.

## Two things I noticed and did NOT touch

- `CLAUDE.md` states the suite is **202 passed, 1 skipped**; it is 206 before my change and 207 after — stale from the panels that landed this chapter, and b1/b2 will move it again. I left it alone deliberately: it is a magnet for a three-way conflict while three cards are in flight, and its own advice is to prefer a re-runnable command over a number. Worth one docs card at the end of the chapter, together with the "eight sections are stubs" paragraph, which is also no longer true.
- `-diff` means `git diff` reports the bundle as binary rather than printing 190kb of minified output. Deliberate and I think right (the rebuild is the change, the bytes are not reviewable), but it is a visible behaviour change — `git log -p` on a UI commit now says "Binary files differ". `git diff --exit-code`, `--name-only` and `--stat` all still work, so `npm run check`'s closure is unaffected. Say the word and I will drop `-diff` and keep only `-merge`; nothing else depends on it.

card.spec:
The hook delivers a pending MENTION and nothing else. The gap it leaves is the orchestrator's: over ten turns of Edit and Bash the board accumulates work that is finished-and-invisible or owned-and-dead, and nothing reaches the human until they think to look.

**This is not hypothetical and the evidence is on this board.** On 2026-08-08 the orchestrator dispatched tk-342486 and tk-17d463 and never spawned their workers. Both sat `stalled` for twelve minutes — correctly derived, correctly displayed, and unread. BERNA caught it from the dashboard; the orchestrator did not. `assign` prepares and starts nothing, and that gap between the two is where a whole wave can quietly stop.

## What binds you, and it is most of the card

Read `src/taskops/cli/claude.py` first — its docstring is the contract, and the four properties it lists are each a test. Then MENTIONS.md §9 and ARCHITECTURE.md §11. The rule is not "no hooks", it is:

    a hook may DELIVER — it may never decide, never store, never write.

Concretely, and all of these are refusals, not preferences:
- **EXTEND the one hook. Do not add a second.** CLAUDE.md says one exists and only one; two entry points is how v1 came to disagree with itself.
- **The read must not renew.** `mentions` exists precisely because `board` opens with `live.renew(actor)` — right for a call an actor typed, catastrophic for a hook, because renewing on somebody's behalf keeps a dead worker's card out of STALLED. That is a stored `doing` grown back by the side door. Whatever read you use must have the same property; say which you used and prove it does not renew.
- **It decides nothing.** It never assigns, never merges, never spawns. It says what is waiting and names the call; the human acts.
- **Deleting the file loses immediacy and nothing else.** The groups still derive, the board still shows them.
- **Never break the caller, never block, always exit 0**, silence on every failure path.

## What to deliver, and to whom

Only to a `dev:` actor — these are the orchestrator's moves; a worker neither merges nor dispatches, and delivering them to one is noise it cannot act on. The groups that qualify are the ones the board's own docstring ranks as somebody-must-move: MERGE (done, not integrated), REVIEW (handed in, nobody checking), STALLED (owned, nobody running it). Not TAKE and not DOING — ready work is a plan, not a thing going wrong.

Throttle it like the mention half is throttled, and make the interval fit the failure: a mention is urgent within a turn, a stalled card is not — twelve minutes of silence was the real incident, so a look every few minutes is plenty and a look per tool call is noise. Say nothing at all when there is nothing to say, which must remain the common case.

The wording matters as much as the mechanism: one line per group with the count and the exact call that clears it, in the order the board already ranks them. A reader who sees it mid-turn must be able to act without opening anything else.

Python only — no bundle rebuild, no .tsx.

Event stream is drawn to its full shape and shows nothing, because no verb returns the log. This card is the verb, the paging, and the wiring — one vertical slice on purpose: splitting the Python from the .tsx is precisely the seam this project has been bitten by twice (`docs/fan-out.md`).

## What the pane's own builder specified

Read the close note on tk-4b37dd first — the worker who drew the pane wrote the spec for the verb it needs, and it is concrete: return `Event[]` as stored (`id · task · actor · kind · body · ts`, INCLUDING `task="project"` rows — a commit made outside any card is board history and must not vanish), newest first, plus the log's total length for the counter above the pane. Its `FIXTURE_EVENTS` is already the real `KINDS` vocabulary and is exported for exactly this moment.

## Page by `seq`, not by `ts`

That note proposed `before=<ts>`. Prefer `seq`: `store/cache.py`'s DDL makes it `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, so it is unique, monotonic and the rowid — a reverse scan is free and needs no new index. `ts` ties (two events in one instant, which this board produces constantly) and skews between machines; a cursor that can tie can skip or repeat a row at a page boundary. Say this in the code where somebody will later be tempted to "fix" it back to a timestamp.

The cache needs ONE new method — `WHERE seq < ? ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT ?` — beside `since()` and `window()`, and SQL lives only in `store/` (`test_architecture` enforces it). `count()` already answers the total.

## The verb

A READ, in `verbs/`, registered in the registry with `BOTH` roles. Decide and state: does it renew the lease? `board` and `report` do (the call IS the heartbeat); `mentions` deliberately does not, because a hook calls it on somebody else's behalf. This one is called by a human reading a page — argue it either way but argue it.

**Milestone filtering is a real decision, not an oversight**: the pane sits in Monitor's chapter-focused column, but an event knows its `task`, not its chapter, and `task="project"` rows belong to no chapter at all. Choose — unfiltered log, or filtered with project-level rows always kept — and write down why. Do not filter silently.

## The client

`RpcVerb` in `ui/src/types.ts` gains it (that union is what makes inventing a verb a compile error), with its `@source` line and an `EventPage` type transcribed from what the verb actually returns.

`useBoard` is the ONE owner of "what does the board say right now" and must stay that: the log is paginated and cannot ride a snapshot, so this is a SECOND read, not a second socket. Recommended shape — the pane owns its pages, the existing feed signal resets it to page one, and nothing here opens another socket. State what you built.

Paging in the pane: it already has the design's `max-height: 620px; overflow-y: auto`. Load the next page from the bottom — button or scroll, your call, but a page boundary must never drop or duplicate a row, and prove that with a test at a boundary rather than by inspection.

The empty state stays for a board that genuinely has no events; what must go is the sentence saying no verb exists.

You own the rebuild of your own bundle — the chapter-close rebuild has already run, so `node build.mjs` from ui/ and commit `src/taskops/ui/`, verifying the other views' markers survive and the bundle only grows.

body.goal: GitHub is the viewer; taskops is the board. Cards read like PRs (base ms/<slug>, head tk-xxx) and milestones like PR groups — but taskops never hosts, serves or replicates git content. Three mechanisms: (1) commit events carry numstat so every dev sees +/- per file through the board channel that already syncs; (2) branches reach `origin` by best-effort pushes at the three lifecycle moments that already exist (done, integrate, land — trees.py:121 is the precedent and its comment is the contract: best effort, local still lands); (3) the board records the repo's GitHub slug once, written by the side that has the repo, so every dashboard — local or remote — links to github.com/<slug>/commit/<sha> and /compare/ms...tk. The switch for ALL of it is `git remote get-url origin`, never local-vs-remote mode: without origin nothing pushes, no links render, and nothing degrades — that is today's taskops, unchanged.
rules: LOCAL == REMOTE BY CONSTRUCTION. The dashboard renders the board; a git fact enters the board only as an EVENT, written by the side that has the repo (hooks, init/join, the MCP layer). No verb touches git (test_architecture enforces it), no server reads a repo, no filesystem peeking from the UI. If a feature needs the repo at render time, it is designed wrong.

PUSH IS BEST-EFFORT, NEVER A GATE AND NEVER IN A COMMIT HOOK. trees.py:121 is the pattern: `# best effort; local still landed`. A failed push changes nothing about the board action that triggered it; offline is a normal state, not an error. Never break the caller, never block.
NO ORIGIN, NO FEATURE, NO NOISE: every piece switches on `git remote get-url origin` (or the slug's presence in the payload), silently. A board without a remote behaves byte-for-byte like today.

The event log stores REFERENCES AND MEASURES (sha, subject, numstat), never content. Patches, trees and blame live in git and are viewed on GitHub — events.jsonl is replayed forever and has no delete.

The wave convention from the Monitor chapter holds: UI cards ship .ts/.tsx-only diffs, npm run typecheck as gate, one chapter-close card rebuilds and commits the bundle. Python cards run ./scripts/lint && ./scripts/test (baseline 222 passed, no skips — re-derive, do not trust). Commit BEFORE mutation-checking. Throwaway probes carry the card id in their filename — the scratchpad is shared.

Version skew is load-bearing: every new payload key is optional in ui/src/types.ts with its @source line, and every consumer has a fallback — three real crashes came from asserting keys an older board does not send.

card.spec:
Berna, reading the dashboard: *"lo que me llama la atención es que ya no puedo ver el capítulo anterior, debería poder revisar todo, ahora desapareció"*. He is right, and it is a regression this project introduced yesterday.

`pulse.py:134` sends `[m for m in milestones if m["status"] == "open"]`. That was correct when `open` was the only status a milestone ever had. Yesterday's fold fix made `landed` real (`core/replay.py::_milestone`, so `open_milestone` would stop degrading forever) — and the same day, two finished chapters vanished from the dashboard: 14 cards and 22 cards, their goals, their rules, their whole threads. Verified in the log right now:

    landed  14 cards  UI — React dashboard (Nova)
    landed  22 cards  Monitor — Nova, panel by panel
    open     7 cards  GitHub-visible — the board points at the code

Nothing was lost — the log has it all — but no screen can reach it. **This is the same bug as `groups.done`**, which Berna also found by looking at the screen: a merged card used to leave the payload entirely and a chapter's finished work existed on no screen. That was fixed for CARDS and left broken for CHAPTERS.

## What to build

The payload must be able to answer for a landed chapter, and the dashboard must be able to reach one. Concretely, and each is a judgement to state:

1. **`milestones` in the board payload.** Sending every chapter forever is unbounded the way `groups.done` was — so decide: all of them (chapters are few, unlike events), the open ones plus the most recent N landed, or open plus a count. Whatever you choose, the CHOSEN chapter (`milestone=`) must resolve even when it is landed — `_which()` looks it up by id and does not filter, so check that path holds.
2. **The milestone picker** (`components/chrome/MilestonePicker.tsx`) must offer landed chapters, visibly distinct from open ones — a reader must never confuse "finished" with "in flight". It already carries an "all chapters" entry; landed ones belong under it, not mixed in.
3. **The panes must survive a landed chapter in focus**: every group is empty, `done` carries its cards, Chapter in focus shows its goal, rules, criteria and branch. Check each pane's empty state reads correctly for "this chapter is finished" rather than "nothing is happening" — Live leases saying `0 ready to pick up` is honest but reads as a live board; say what you did.
4. **`groups.done` is capped at 20** (`pulse.DONE_SHOWN`) and Monitor's chapter had 22. Reviewing a landed chapter is exactly when somebody wants ALL of them. Decide: raise the cap when a milestone is explicitly focused, page it, or leave it and show the honest "20 of 22" that already exists. Argue it.

Version skew applies as always: any new/changed payload key is optional in `ui/src/types.ts` with its `@source` line, consumers fall back, no assertions.

This card crosses the wire (pulse.py + the picker + panes). It ships .ts/.tsx-only for the UI half per the wave convention — the chapter-close card rebuilds.

1. BOUNDING. `milestones` = every OPEN chapter + the `LANDED_SHOWN = 20` most recent landed, newest first, plus `landed_total`. card.spec:
The whole Python half, serialized — the UI card builds on the wire shape this card fixes, so this lands first and alone.

**1. `gitwork/diff.py`** (new; gitwork is the ONLY git). Two readers:
- `stat(repo, a, b)` → the numstat between two refs — same `{path: [added, deleted] | null}` shape `bind.py` already writes, null for binary, so the UI has ONE vocabulary for +/- everywhere.
- `patch(repo, a, b, path=None, cap=…)` → unified diff text, whole range or one file, truncated at a byte cap WITH a `truncated: true` flag — a silently-cut patch is a lie; a flagged one is a fact.
Both validate refs FIRST via `git rev-parse --verify --quiet` through `gitwork/run` — a ref is an opaque token handed to git as an argv element, never interpolated, and an unknown ref is a clean None/refusal before any diff runs. Commit case is `sha^!`-style (a commit against its first parent) — decide the exact spelling and state it; merge commits must not explode into the whole branch's diff.

**2. The `/git` door in `http/`.** Mounted ONLY when the host sits inside a repo. Read `http/mounts.py` first: `taskops ui` constructs the server with `root = <repo>/.taskops` (the repo is `root.parent`), `taskops serve` with a boards directory that has no repo — that existing difference IS the switch; make it explicit (a `repo: Path | None` on Mounts or equivalent), never a heuristic re-derived per request. Routes — keep them boring and REST-less like /rpc:
- `GET /<board>/git/commit/<sha>` → {stat, patch?, truncated}
- `GET /<board>/git/compare/<a>...<b>` → same shape for a range (the card-as-PR read: ms-branch...tk-branch)
Same token auth as everything else (`auth.py`), same envelope discipline as rpc.py (always an object, errors as {ok:false, error}), 404 with a stated reason on a repo-less host — the UI treats that as "this host has no repo", so the words matter.

**3. The amendment**, in this card because this card is the decision: rewrite ARCHITECTURE.md §16's invariant paragraph to its new form — the dashboard renders the board, plus git content served by a host that sits inside a repo; ui mounts /git, serve does not and says so; the asymmetry is honest because every dev has a clone by construction (board.json lives in the repo) and only a clone-less browser ever meets the gap, where the cascade falls to the slug link or an honest sentence.

Tests: ref validation (bad ref → refusal, no subprocess explosion), the cap (over-cap → truncated flag), the mount switch (serve-rooted server answers 404 with the stated reason, ui-rooted answers), and the commit-vs-compare shapes. Mutation-check the validation especially — an injection-shaped mutation must fail a test.

body.goal: The dashboard shows real diffs — commit patches and card-as-PR file lists — served by the viewer's OWN host from the viewer's OWN clone. The insight the design rests on: every dev has the repo by construction (board.json lives inside it; you cannot even join without a checkout), so "the side that has the repo" at render time is always the viewer's machine. `taskops ui` sits inside a repo and mounts a read-only /git door; `taskops serve` sits in a boards directory, mounts nothing, and fakes nothing — the only viewer that ever hits that gap is a browser with no clone (a phone), where the fallback is the GitHub link if a slug exists, else an honest sentence. This AMENDS the GitHub-visible chapter's invariant ("no server reads a repo") and the amendment is written into ARCHITECTURE.md §16 explicitly, not smuggled: the dashboard renders the board, PLUS git content served by a host that sits inside a repo; a host that does not, says so.
rules: The amendment is explicit or it does not happen: ARCHITECTURE.md §16's invariant is rewritten to name the /git door, which host mounts it (ui: yes — it sits in a repo; serve: no — it sits in a boards directory), and why the asymmetry is honest (every dev has a clone; only a clone-less browser ever meets the gap). A reader must be able to tell this was DECIDED.

The /git door is READ-ONLY and refuses before it runs: refs are validated (a sha or a branch name the repo actually has — `git rev-parse --verify` through gitwork/run, never string interpolation into a command), responses are size-capped with the cap stated in the payload, and every failure is a clean refusal, never a traceback. Same token auth as /rpc — no second credential system.
git stays in gitwork/, SQL stays in store/, verbs stay git-free — test_architecture is the referee and imports point down (http→5 → gitwork→4 is legal, the same edge mcp/ already uses).
events.jsonl still stores references and measures, never content. The /git door DERIVES from the repo on demand; nothing it returns is ever written to the board.

The UI falls back in one declared cascade and no other: numstat from the event → patch from /git → GitHub link via slug → one honest sentence. No dead anchors, no empty panes pretending, no layout shift between states.

Wave conventions hold: UI cards ship .ts/.tsx-only diffs (npm run typecheck as gate, npm ci first if node_modules is absent), ONE chapter-close card rebuilds and commits the bundle, Python cards keep ./scripts/lint && ./scripts/test green (re-derive the count — do not trust a number from a brief), commit BEFORE mutation-checking, probes carry the card id in their filename, every new payload key is optional in types.ts with its @source line and a fallback at every consumer.

═══ THE WIRE SHAPE — transcribe from here ═══

GET /<board>/git/commit/<ref>            ?path=<file> optional
GET /<board>/git/compare/<a>...<b>       ?path=<file> optional
Auth: same token door as /rpc — Authorization: Bearer <t> OR ?token=<t>.

SUCCESS (200) — identical shape for commit and compare, one renderer:
{"ok": true, "seq": 0, "data": {
  "base": "<40-hex sha>",        // first parent, or merge-base, or EMPTY_TREE
  "head": "<40-hex sha>",
  "stat": {"path/to/file.py": [added, deleted], "logo.png": null},
  "patch": "<unified diff text>",
  "truncated": false,
  "cap": 524288                  // bytes; diff.CAP
}}
`stat` is EXACTLY bind.py's numstat vocabulary: [added, deleted], null for a binary, never [0,0]. Same keys as `files` in a commit event.

FAILURE — rpc.py envelope, always an object:
{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}

- 404 not_found, host with no repo (THE cascade trigger — UI matches on these words):
  "this host serves boards, not a repository — it was started outside a checkout (taskops serve), so there is no clone here to read a diff from. A host that sits in a repo (taskops ui) answers /git."
- 404 not_found, unknown ref: "this repo has no commit 'does-not-exist'"
  compare form: "this repo does not have both 'a' and 'b'"
- 400 bad_request, malformed route: "git/commit/<ref> or git/compare/<a>...<b>"
- 409 refused, no token: "no credential — run: taskops join <url with ?token= or ?invite=>"

═══ THE MERGE-COMMIT SPELLING, chosen and stated ═══

`git diff <sha>^1 <sha>` — first parent resolved BY NAME via rev-parse, not `sha^!` and not a bare `git show`.
`sha^!` expands to `sha --not sha^@`, excluding EVERY parent: on a merge the patch becomes the whole merged branch, so every landed card would render as the diff of its entire chapter. First parent only is also what GitHub shows for a merge.
Root commit (no parent) → git's own empty tree 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 (diff.EMPTY_TREE). "No parent" is not "no diff".
Compare = merge-base(a, b) → b, resolved explicitly with `git merge-base` rather than written `a...b`, so the two-dot/three-dot ambiguity is never something a reader has to remember.

═══ REF VALIDATION — the security boundary ═══
Two walls, then the string is DROPPED:
1. shape guard `usable()` — refuses empty, anything starting with `-` (an argv element read as an OPTION is the one way it still misbehaves), and anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_/.^~@{}+-]{1,200}
2. `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}` via gitwork/run (list argv, no shell anywhere in the package), result must fullmatch [0-9a-f]{40}
From there ONLY the resolved sha reaches a diff command — the browser's string cannot get there even in principle. `?path=` goes after `--`.
`ms/the-chapter` still resolves: the guard is not so tight it refuses taskops' own branch shape (pinned).

MUTATION-CHECKED, ONE SITE AT A TIME, after committing — 9 mutants, all red:
M1 drop shape guard → 4 injection cases red (rev-parse alone catches the rest — defence in depth, and now measured)
M2 allow leading `-` → injection[-o] red
M3 resolve returns the raw ref instead of the sha → 2 red
M4 `^1` → `^@` → merge-first-parent + numstat red
M5 drop EMPTY_TREE fallback → root-commit + door red
M6 truncated flag True→False → cap test red
M7 drop `--` before path → path-filter red
M8 gitdoor repo None → Path.cwd() → mount-switch red
M9 drop the credential check in _git → token-door red

M7 exposed a real defect in my own test: the mutant wrote /tmp/tk-d50e0a-pwned for REAL and the leftover file poisoned the next two runs. Fixed in b511a7e — the hostile output path is under tmp_path, and M7 re-run red with the fixed test.

TESTS — homes chosen, no new file needed:
- tests/test_git.py (its `repo()` fixture already builds real repos, "no mocks: git is the point"): 12 tests incl. a parametrized injection sweep of 10 hostile refs, plus a `merged()` helper that builds a REAL merge where main also moved, which is what discriminates first-parent from the whole branch.

FOR THE UI CARD (tk-e586f5): the cascade's step-2 fetch is `/<board>/git/commit/<sha>?path=<file>` for the dossier's per-file diff; step-2 for card-as-PR is `/<board>/git/compare/ms%2F<slug>...tk-<id>`. card.spec:
THE BUG, reproduced and diagnosed — you do not have to find it, only fix it. Every worktree in the dashboard says `no files differ between ms/<chapter> and tk-<id>`. Verified in this repo:

    $ git merge-base ms/worktrees-the-tree-as-a-pull-req tk-c4445b   → 941a75c
    $ git rev-parse tk-c4445b                                        → 941a75c
    $ git merge-base --is-ancestor tk-c4445b ms/worktrees-…          → true
    $ git diff --numstat 941a75c 941a75c                             → 0 files

`gitwork/diff.py::compare_range` returns `(merge-base(a, b), b)`. That is exactly right while a card is IN FLIGHT. The moment it is integrated, its branch holds nothing the chapter branch does not, the merge-base IS the head, and the range is empty. Not an error — the correct answer to the wrong question. Every card of a closed chapter is in that state, which is why it looks like the feature never worked.

THE FIX, one rule: **when `head` is already an ancestor of `base`, the base is not the merge-base — it is the FIRST PARENT of the merge commit that brought `head` in.** `taskops_merge` integrates with `--no-ff` (gitwork/trees.py), so that commit always exists for a card this board integrated, and its first parent is the chapter branch as it stood immediately before. This is the same view GitHub shows for a merged pull request. Verified here:

    $ M=$(git rev-list --ancestry-path --merges tk-c4445b..ms/worktrees-… | tail -1)
    → 20d7b5a  "merge tk-c4445b"
    $ git diff --numstat 20d7b5a^1 tk-c4445b   → 3 files

NOTHING IS STORED. No event, no payload key, no verb, no cache — the fact is in the commit graph and is derived on demand, which is ARCHITECTURE.md §16's whole rule for this door. Do not reach for the `merged` event's sha even though it exists: this module knows nothing about a board and must not start to.

WHERE: `compare_range`, and only there. Every caller (`http/gitdoor.py`, `between`, `stat`, `patch`) already takes a resolved pair and keeps working unchanged. Keep the existing behaviour byte-for-byte for a card in flight — that path must not move.

THE SECURITY CONTRACT DOES NOT BEND. Both refs still come through `resolve()` first, only 40-hex shas are handed to any further command, and the new `rev-list` call takes them as separate argv elements through `gitwork/run.py` like everything else in this module.

THE HONEST FALLBACK. If `head` is an ancestor of `base` and NO merge commit is found on the ancestry path (a fast-forward integration, which this board does not do but another clone might), return what it returns today — the empty range. An empty diff that is true beats a guessed base. Say so in a comment.

Extend the module docstring's "compare case" paragraph: it currently says the range is `merge-base(a, b) → b` and that is now half the rule. Write the post-mortem in the docstring the way this codebase does — what the screen said, why the answer was correct and useless, and what decides the base now.

TESTS: `tests/test_gitwork.py`. Build a real repo with a branch, merge it `--no-ff`, and assert the compare range is non-empty AFTER the merge and names the merge commit's first parent; assert the in-flight case is unchanged; assert the fast-forward case returns the empty range rather than inventing one. Mutation-check ONE site at a time.

body.reason:
Fixed in compare_range only; every caller unchanged. b3e268a. ./scripts/lint clean, ./scripts/test 285 passed, 1 skipped (the ui harness half — npm ci not run in this worktree; baseline here was 282+1, I added 3 tests).

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE SPEC, measured, please read. The spec said the base is the merge commit's FIRST PARENT. I implemented merge-base(first parent, head) instead — anchored on the same merge commit, but never ahead of the card's branch point. Reason: on this repo's real branches the bare first parent is wrong for most cards, because a chapter integrates card after card, so by the time a card lands its chapter tip already carries its SIBLINGS' work, which the card branch never had — and `git diff` is symmetric, so all of it renders as the card DELETING files it never touched. Measured across every tk-* branch: tk-17d463 reads 24 files from the bare first parent vs 7 from the merge-base of it; tk-342486 17 vs 3; tk-097cae 21 vs 13. The spec's own verified case, tk-c4445b against ms/worktrees-the-tree-as-a-pull-req, still returns exactly the 3 files it states — when no sibling landed in between the two commits are identical, which is why the spec's single sample did not show it. This is what GitHub shows for a merged PR (base...head, three-dot). Criteria 1's intent is met; its literal wording is not, and that is deliberate — the docstring carries the numbers and the reasoning.

The diff page works and is unreadable. Four things, and the third is the real work.

1. IT IS SIZED FOR A DRAWER. `components/card/Patch.tsx::pane` is `fontSize: 11.5px`, `maxHeight: 360px`, `lineHeight: 1.55` — chosen for a 900px dossier column, and on a full-width page it is a ribbon in the middle of nothing. The patch pane needs a PAGE's measurements: ~13px mono, a max height that is a fraction of the viewport rather than a fixed 360px, more room per file, and file rows that read as headers instead of list items. Do NOT change how it looks inside the drawer — the dossier keeps its pane exactly as it is today. Make the size a PROP or a variant with two named values (`"drawer" | "page"`), defaulted to `drawer`, so no existing caller moves and the choice is declared rather than inherited from context.

2. TWO COLUMNS, side by side, with a toggle. This is the piece with actual thinking in it and it belongs in a NEW pure module, `ui/src/components/card/split.ts`, so it is testable with no DOM at all:

       split(patch: string): Hunk[]
       Hunk  = { header: string; rows: Row[] }
       Row   = { left: {n: number, text: string} | null,
                 right: {n: number, text: string} | null }

   The grammar is the one `Patch.tsx::tone` already reads and nothing more: `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` opens a hunk and gives both starting line numbers; ` ` is a context row (both sides, both numbers advance); `-` is left only; `+` is right only; a RUN of `-` followed by a run of `+` pairs up positionally — the first deletion beside the first addition — and whichever run is longer leaves `null` on the other side for its tail. `+++`/`---`/`diff `/`index `/`new file`/`deleted file` are file headers and belong to no hunk. Anything it cannot parse is NOT rendered as an empty table: `split` returns `[]` and the component falls back to the unified view it already draws. That fallback is the whole safety of this feature.

   The toggle lives on the diff PAGE (unified ↔ split), remembers nothing, and defaults to SPLIT — it is the reason the page exists. Both sides scroll together on one X axis; a long line must never make the page itself scroll horizontally, which is the one failure mode `Patch.tsx`'s header already names.

A worktree has no identity apart from its card — `gitwork/trees.py` pins `tk-<id>` as branch, directory and id at once — so there is NO worktree comment and there must never be one: a second thread would be two places to say something about one thing, and the reader of the card would not see half of it. HONOUR THAT LITERALLY. No verb, no payload key, no store, no second fetch, no socket. Everything below is already on `BoardPayload`:

  NODES
    orchestrator   — `dev:…` from `team`; never holds a card (the role rule)

    contested      — a DASHED edge between two cards that declare a file in common (`BoardRow.files`).

card.spec:
Opening an actor on the Actors view shows WHEN it worked — a Harvest-style timesheet — and, beside it, why the total is the number it is.

THE DATA ALREADY EXISTS INSIDE THE ARITHMETIC. `core/hours.py::spent` walks consecutive events per actor, credits each interval ≤ GAP to the card of the event that CLOSES it, and then throws the intervals away, keeping only sums. This card exposes them — it does not compute a second time.

    sessions(stamps) -> list[Session]      Session = {start, end, task, seconds}

AND `spent()` MUST BE RE-EXPRESSED IN TERMS OF IT, so there is exactly ONE definition of what an interval is. Two functions each deciding what counts is how the totals and the timeline drift into disagreeing on screen, and the drift would be invisible until somebody added them up by hand. The existing tests for `spent` must pass UNCHANGED afterwards — if one has to move, that is a signal you changed the meaning, not the shape; stop and say so.

A SESSION IS A RUN OF INTERVALS, not one interval: consecutive events on the SAME card with no dropped gap between them are one block. A gap over GAP ends the block and starts a new one. Two events on different cards end a block too — the timeline's blocks are per card, because "what was it working on at 15:40" is the question this answers.

WHAT THE DROPPED TIME IS. Between the end of one session and the start of the next there is time that is deliberately NOT counted (`GAP`, and the post-mortem in the module docstring: v1 capped it at 30 min and every break added a phantom half hour). That gap must be VISIBLE — as space on the timeline, and as a figure: how many gaps and how much wall-clock they hold. A timesheet that only draws the counted time silently claims the rest did not happen.

THE VERB. `verbs/report.py` carries the sessions per actor for the window it is already computing — the same events, the same pass, no second query and no new store. Cap what travels if a long window would make this list unbounded, and if you cap it SAY the total beside it (`done_total`'s pattern). Key OPTIONAL in `ui/src/types.ts` with its @source line.

THE SCREEN. Opening an actor — any actor, a `dev:` included — reveals its timesheet in place; it is not a modal and not a second page (this dashboard's drawer belongs to a CARD, and an actor is not one). Per day in the window:

    09:12 ──██████────██████████───────────████── 18:40      3h 10m worked
           tk-a11ffa    tk-d34294               tk-f0aa12       2 gaps · 1h 40m not counted

Blocks are positioned by real time, so two actors' rows can be compared by eye — THAT is how "who was working in parallel" gets answered, and it is why the day's axis must be shared across actors rather than each row scaling to its own extent. A block names its card and opens that card's dossier when activated (`openCard`, the same one every view uses); the empty space between blocks is not clickable and carries the gap figure in its title.

AND THE CALCULATION, ON SCREEN. Somewhere on the actor's detail, in the design system's quiet ink, the rule in one or two sentences: the signal is the timestamps of the events themselves, an interval is credited to the card that CLOSES it, and a gap longer than 30 minutes is dropped whole rather than capped. Lift the wording from `core/hours.py`'s own docstring rather than writing a second explanation that can drift from it. This is the difference between a number somebody trusts and a number somebody argues with.

EMPTY IS REAL: an actor with no events in the window has no timesheet, and says that, rather than an empty axis.

card.spec:
THE BUG, measured on this board's own log:

    status done: 61 · con reason: 61

Every single close carries the worker's note. `verbs/update.py::_transition` writes it as `body["reason"]` on a `status` event, and `mcp/thread.py::detail` renders it — `: done — <the note>`. An agent reading the card by MCP sees it. **The dashboard does not.**

WHY. `Thread.tsx::text()` pulls the line out of an untyped body by trying keys in order:

    for (const key of ["text", "note", "to", "subject", "into", "verdict"])

`reason` is not in that list, and `to` IS — so a close resolves to the string `"done"`, the loop stops, and the prose is never reached. Then the render only draws a text block when `event.kind === "comment"`, so even the right string would not appear. Two independent reasons, both must go.

THE REAL DEFECT is that this thread has TWO renderers and only one of them is right: `mcp/thread.py::detail` (Python, correct — it has a dedicated `status` branch that reads `reason` OR `note`, adds `(no code)`, and appends the prose after an em dash) and `Thread.tsx` (TypeScript, wrong). They cannot share code across the language boundary, so the fix is to make the TS one MIRROR the Python one branch for branch, and to say so in the file's docstring naming `mcp/thread.py::detail` as the thing it must agree with. A reader who changes one now knows there is a second.

WHAT TO RENDER. A `status` event shows its transition AND its note, and the note is prose — same treatment a comment's text gets (the Markdown renderer, the same ink, the same width), because a close note is the most substantial writing on most cards and it is what this whole complaint is about. Keep the kind pill and the `to` value where they are: the reader must still see at a glance that this was a close and not a remark.

DO IT FOR EVERY EVENT THAT CARRIES PROSE, not only `done`: `released` and `submitted` write `body["note"]`, a review verdict writes its own, `dropped` writes `reason` — and the cancel reason is REQUIRED by the server, so it can never be legitimately empty. Walk `verbs/` and `core/review.py`, list the bodies that carry human text, and cover them. Say in your close note which kinds you covered and which you found carry none.

`no_code` rides on the same body and today is invisible on screen too — the Python renderer prints `(no code)`. It means a card closed with no commit bound to it, which is exactly the kind of thing a reader should not have to open the log to learn.

Do not change what is STORED, do not add a payload key, do not touch the Python. The data has been right all along.

Pin it in `ui/smoke/main.tsx` from the server's own payload: a `status` `done` with a reason renders the reason; one with `no_code` says so; a `released` renders its note. And extend the marker row in `tests/test_ui.py` so the shipped bundle is checked too. Mutation-check ONE site at a time, committing first and restoring with `git checkout -- <file>` (`cp` is aliased to `cp -i` here).

Do not rebuild the committed bundle — tk-56740f does it once at the end of this chapter.

card.spec:
SERIALIZED FIRST — everything else in this chapter builds on the identity this card creates.

TWO THINGS, and the second closes a known security hole.

1. A SERVER-LEVEL IDENTITY STORE. Today identity lives per board (`store/creds.py` in each board's live.sqlite) and the server as a whole knows nobody — which is WHY admin falls to ssh. Add `<root>/server.sqlite` (a new `store/server.py`; the only-SQL-in-store rule holds) with: principals (name, role owner|member, created), and their PUBKEYS (the key line, a fingerprint, created, revoked). Alongside it, MAINTAIN `<root>/allowed_signers` — the exact file format `ssh-keygen -Y verify` consumes (`principal key-type key`) — regenerated from the store on every change, never hand-edited. The store is the truth; the file is a derived artifact for the verifier, same pattern as cache.sqlite.

   `taskops server init --root <dir>` bootstraps: takes the owner's pubkey (a path or stdin), writes the first principal as OWNER. This is the ONE act that happens over ssh, ever, and the docstring says why: trust has to enter the system through some prior channel, and the machine's own shell is that channel.

2. NO BOARD WITHOUT A VERB. `mounts.stores()` today does `Stores(self.root / name)` for ANY name matching the pattern — BEFORE auth — which means an anonymous request can create a board directory on disk (found 2026-08-08, deliberately left unprobed). Kill it: mounting only ever OPENS a directory that already exists; an unknown board answers 404 with no side effect, pinned by a test that requests a nonsense name and then proves the directory does NOT exist. Creation becomes an explicit server-scope operation (the verb arrives in the admin card; this card makes creation-by-accident impossible first).
